Situation: ATL is running on 2 of 4 runways (22L and 22R closed for weather, +1 min landing spacing, arrival capacity 22/h), with 10 other arrivals already sequenced on 28R and 28L, and one flight, DL1814, to place.

DL1814 (CRITICAL): lands 21:51 on runway 28R, standard route (STD), gate B2 (gate-in 22:02), no holding. Fuel at landing 35 min vs 30 min reserve, so 5 min above reserve.

Binding constraint: DL1814 is the binding flight. Its earliest possible landing is 21:51, and it lands at exactly that time, so no slot could have been earlier. Its CRITICAL priority (5 min fuel margin over reserve, and only 5 min turnaround slack on its next leg) protects it from being pushed later, but the time itself is set by how soon it can physically reach the runway. Any delay would eat into a 5 min fuel margin.

Main trade-off: DL1814 was given its earliest slot with zero holding, so the 10 already-sequenced arrivals on 28R and 28L had to be fitted around it under the reduced capacity and extra spacing. The cost to the rest of the flow is not quantified in the data. For DL1814 itself there is no cost: 0 connections missed (of 31 connecting), 0 crew overtime, 0 next-leg delay.

How it was decided: consensus, reached in 2 rounds. No fallback was needed.
